chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who recognizes the differing of the people, so he is not a weak one (of understanding).

key_terms.مُسْتَضْعَف: Weak, weak-minded, or lacking in strength/understanding

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be not weak in understanding according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from al-Kafi highlights that intellectual resilience stems from recognizing the diversity of human thought and behavior, preventing one from being easily swayed or deemed 'weak' in understanding. It underscores the virtue of critical awareness and adaptability in navigating social and theological complexities, a key trait for the discerning believer.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Al Magra’a, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who recognises the differing of the people, so he is not a weak one (of understanding)’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu al- Maghra’ from abu Basir from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Whoever knows the differences among people is not a feeble- minded person.”
